places.name: The Held Breath
sources: module 20 §12.3b hard-to-reach types (underwater grottoes, air pockets, flooded cellars)
uesp:Lore:Argonian (amphibious physiology; the crossing is priced around held breath)

why.founding: A maintained air pocket on a flooded root route, kept so the crossing is survivable.
why.siteAdvantages: The midpoint of the longest flooded branch in the region.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody lives here; it is maintained by whoever passes, on an interior custom that a shelter you use unrepaired is a shelter you have stolen.
why.pressures: The seal leaks and the pocket is smaller each decade. The Waykeepers who could reseal it will not work outside a paid line.
why.wouldChangeIf: Losing it makes the flooded route impassable. Every crossing then goes by the long root gallery, a day longer and a band of danger worse.

preferences: water relation: fully enclosed by water
neighbours: inside a drowned or flooded place

places.traversalFallback: walk the surface route (two days, D5 ground)

places.name: Alten Markmont
sources: Lore:Alten Markmont (Arena gazetteer); Lore:East Empire Company

why.founding: An outsider-facing trading station built where the southern water route met the Helstrom approach; the alten- prefix marks it as never Argonian.
why.siteAdvantages: A landing on deep-enough water at the last point outsiders were tolerated.
why.occupantsMotive: A skeleton staff of two factors and whoever is sheltering in the warehouses. The two factors are paid a retainer by a company that no longer trades here, on the theory that a lapsed post is cheaper to hold than to re-license.
why.pressures: The interior tolerates it but does not need it. The trade it was built for stopped. The warehouses now shelter people the factors are not allowed to register.
why.wouldChangeIf: A single busy season would refill it. The Helstrom assembly has decided there will not be one.

preferences: water relation: on a navigable route inland
neighbours: too far inland for its own logistics

places.name: Thousand-Chimes
sources: Lore:Bright-Throat Village; Lore:Argonian (jewellery, guarded weaving secrets)

why.founding: A craft village that makes the bone and tin chimes through which half the province listens to its Hist.
why.siteAdvantages: Beside a hero Hist whose wind is reliable. The chimes are tuned against the tree that will hang them.
why.occupantsMotive: Chime-makers whose tuning is a religious qualification, not a trade skill. Tuning is examined and licensed by the tree-minders, so a maker who loses the qualification loses the craft and the village at once.
why.pressures: Cheap cast chimes from the cities are undercutting them and, they say, mistranslating the trees. The tree-minders have declined to rule on that for six years.
why.wouldChangeIf: A ruling that cast chimes are valid would end the village's authority. The coastal foundries would take the province's trade within a decade.

preferences: water relation: within poling reach of a trade channel, though the tuning tree sets the site
neighbours: on a trade water; brokers between neighbours

notableNpcSlots: the chime-maker
the deelith who teaches the trade

why.occupantsMotive: Nothing that talks. The lower rings are dry, which in this region explains everything else that lives there.
why.pressures: Antiquarians want in but the interior tribes have no stake either way. Nobody with a licence has survived the descent.

places.name: Long-Stride

why.founding: The keepers bred lizard-steeds on this rise for two generations before a wet season flooded the schooling paddock and let the breeding stock loose.
why.siteAdvantages: The same firm rise and soft-ground paddock that once suited training now suits a wamasu denned in the flooded pens.
why.occupantsMotive: The wamasu that took the paddock has no reason to leave water this good and this undisturbed.
why.pressures: Porters who once bought steeds here now route wide around the pens. The loss has driven up prices on every interior road.
why.wouldChangeIf: Killing or driving off the wamasu would leave the pens open for breeding again, but nobody has tried since the keepers scattered.

preferences: water relation: penned water separated from open channel
neighbours: supplies mounts or protection to a district

places.name: The Staying Stone
sources: Lore:Wamasu (Haynekhtnamet of Shadowfen received offerings to stop seasonal flooding)

why.occupantsMotive: Nobody lives here. Four villages take turns. The turn order is older than any of their current naheesh.

why.wouldChangeIf: One more bad year and the shrine will be abandoned or rebuilt bigger. Either decision breaks the four-village compact, which is the district's only joint institution.

places.name: Keeps-the-Egg
sources: Lore:Hist (a settlement without a Hist is always political)

why.founding: Their Hist was killed in the Imperial century; the tribe recovered the Mnemic Egg and organised itself around keeping it.
why.siteAdvantages: They did not move. The dead trunk is still the centre of the village and the Egg is kept inside it, reliquary and argument at once.
why.occupantsMotive: Custodians of a memory nobody can currently read.
why.pressures: Three other tribes claim a share of the Egg. One has offered to buy it, publicly, so that refusing would look like hoarding.
why.wouldChangeIf: Reading the Egg, which the main quest's archivists could, would resolve or destroy them. Every claimant tribe knows which outcome it is betting on.

preferences: water relation: as a hist-village
neighbours: neighbours argue about taking them in

notableNpcSlots: the egg-tender who kept the log
the naheesh who will not have the clutch spoken of

places.name: The Lit Fen

why.founding: A fen where the water itself lights at night from Hist-flower fall.
why.siteAdvantages: Still water directly downstream of a hero Hist's grove.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody keeps it. The villages come once a year, on a night fixed by the Tsoko stones. They come in numbers because of what waits in the deep channel.
why.pressures: It only lights while the tree above flowers. This year the light came late and stopped early.
why.wouldChangeIf: The tree failing would put the fen out. That is how the district would learn of it, weeks before the grove admitted anything.

preferences: water relation: still or tidal water, undisturbed

places.name: The Made Ground

why.founding: Xal-Krona are grown by the Hist out of sap, each for a reason. The reason here was the Accord: a sap-flooded hollow where the Hist made the Last Warden. On the evidence lying in it, they did not get it right first time.
why.siteAdvantages: A closed basin fed by deep roots, where sap collects instead of draining. It is the only place in the interior where a tree could pool enough of itself to make something that size.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody lives here. The Warden itself has not been here in an age; it waits in the Lost City, which is what it was made to do. What is here is what was made before it.
why.pressures: The basin still fills each wet season. What it grows now is smaller, wrong and short-lived. The Unbound Root have found the place and read it as a recipe.
why.wouldChangeIf: Reading the making record here first tells you what the Warden was made to test. That is the difference between talking it down and fighting it.

preferences: water relation: enclosed basin
neighbours: within reach of the Lost City approach
reached only through the Lost City: its deepest terrace, never a separate approach

places.name: Xal-Thuun
sources: Lore:Xanmeer (~20% inhabited; inhabited for their walls and still-working ancient defences)

why.founding: A tribe that moved into its ancestors' xanmeer during the Imperial century and never moved out.
why.siteAdvantages: Stone walls and working vakka mechanisms, which make it the strongest fortification in the interior.
why.occupantsMotive: A tribe living in a monument they are supposed only to maintain. They describe the residence as continuous tending to anyone who asks.

why.wouldChangeIf: A mechanism failure would open the strongest position in the region to anyone. The vakka stones that drive it are the largest cache in the interior.
